articles.title: Trump faces backlash after invoking 9/11 in verbal assault on El-Sayed
articles.summary: The Democrat himself has hit back, as has Senator Bernie Sanders and a key Trump supporter from 2024.
articles.body:
Watch: Moment Trump accuses El-Sayed of being a "jihadist"

US President Donald Trump is facing a backlash after invoking 9/11 as part of a verbal assault on Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic candidate for the US Senate in Michigan.

Speaking at a rally in the state on Sunday, Trump accused El-Sayed of being "a jihadist". He introduced as a guest speaker the father of a passenger who fought back against the 9/11 hijackers.

Trump also suggested that El-Sayed would "have to go through a metal detector before he's allowed to go into the Senate".

Critics condemned Trump's attack as Islamophobic. El-Sayed himself responded to Trump's decision to refer to him by his middle name, Mohamed, saying during a rally of his own: "I'll be Senator Mohamed to you, bro."

Watch: The BBC's Sarah Smith asks Democrat El-Sayed about tight Michigan Senate race

He also said: "They think that by pointing at my name and my faith, that somehow you're going to ignore the fact that you can't afford your gas or your groceries, can't see a doctor."

Appearing alongside him, Senator Bernie Sanders said: "The reason they are using Islamophobia against Abdul is because they have nothing to say about the real issues."

El-Sayed is taking on Republican candidate Mike Rogers on 3 November. The race is expected to be one of the closest in the midterm elections, and is proving to be particularly bitter.

The seat is considered to be one of just a handful that could decide the balance of power in Congress. It is currently held by the Democrats.

El-Sayed, a former public health official who was born in the US to Egyptian parents, will be the first Muslim elected to the US Senate if he wins the seat.

He has previously dismissed the various attacks made against him by both Trump and Rogers and denied any connection to extremist groups.

During his remarks on Sunday, Trump said: "If Abdul and the Democrats win, they will open the floodgates and invite hordes of jihadis to our shores, creating a nightmare of violence and terror until you cannot even have a Christmas."

Trump made a variety of allegations against El-Sayed and his family members, including that he was a member of the Muslim Brotherhood.

He introduced as a guest speaker the father of Todd Beamer, a man from Michigan who was part of a group of passengers who fought back against the hijackers of United Airlines Flight 93, before the plane crashed in a field in Pennsylvania.

"Michigan needs to stand up and fight, just like Todd did, to stop a jihadist from walking into the Capitol," Trump said.

Claims centre on proscribed Muslim Brotherhood

El-Sayed's opponents have sought to link him to the Muslim Brotherhood, an Islamist organisation that was founded in Egypt. Trump designated certain chapters of it as Foreign Terrorist Organisations earlier this year.

Some of the scrutiny of the affiliations of El-Sayed and his family members relates to their writings from more than a decade ago.

A social media post in 2012 by El-Sayed's half-sister, Eman Abdelhadi, appeared to refer to the movement, saying "my family has long been MB". El-Sayed's team have previously distanced him from other comments by Abdelhadi.

Critics have also pointed to an opinion piece El-Sayed wrote in Huffington Post in 2011 about pro-democracy protesters in Egypt. In it, he acknowledged concerns that "supporting democracy in Egypt might allow the country to fall to the hands of the Muslim Brotherhood".

A year later he also allegedly signed an open letter by Egyptian Americans. In it, the group urged Mohamed Morsi, Egypt's first democratically elected president and a leader of the Muslim Brotherhood, to "purge the media and police" following the toppling of the authoritarian regime in the Arab Spring. This letter has not been discussed by El-Sayed.

El-Sayed has previously denied any connection to the Muslim Brotherhood and has stressed his loyalty to the United States. Asked recently at a town hall event whether he would disavow the organisation, he responded: "Absolutely."

Also in 2012, El-Sayed's current opponent Rogers, who was then a US representative and chairing the House Intelligence Committee, appeared to call for cautious engagement with the Muslim Brotherhood, telling Reuters : "Do I think there are moderate Muslim Brotherhood individuals we are going to have to reach out to and talk to? Yes but we are going to have to watch it carefully."

HA Hellyer, senior associate fellow at the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI) and an expert on Egypt, says the row has more to do with Islamophobia on the political right in the US than with the Trump administration's actual position on the Muslim Brotherhood.

"If the accusation is to be taken sincerely, then [Trump] should surely have a problem with engaging with any government that has engaged positively with the Brotherhood or with groups that are even more to the right of the Brotherhood," Hellyer told the BBC. "He clearly has not done that."

Watch: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers clash in US Senate debate.

Among the others who condemned Trump's attacks were one of his key supporters ahead of the 2024 presidential election.

"The president's statements are out of line," Bishara Bahbah told the Associated Press. "They are crossing a red line. They are racist."

Bahbah was the founder of Arab Americans for Trump, a group believed to have been important in helping the president connect with a wider range of voters two years ago. The group later changed its name, removing the reference to Trump.

Trump clinched the White House in 2024 after victories in Michigan, which has a prominent population of Arab Americans, and a number of other swing states.

Asked about accusations of Islamophobia, White House spokesman Davis Ingle said: "Abdulrahman Mohamed El-Sayed wants to massively raise taxes, advocates for defunding the police, and wants to destroy the Michigan auto industry by banning gasoline powered vehicles.

"President Trump will continue to call out complete and total extremists like El-Sayed without apology."

Additional reporting by Jake Horton and Tom Bateman

articles.title: Lula será aconselhado a não falar mais em Flávio e dizer que caso é problema do senador com Judiciário | G1
articles.body:
O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) será aconselhado por interlocutores a não falar mais em Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), focar em seu quarto mandato e deixar claro que o problema do senador é com o Judiciário.

Ou seja, o Executivo não tem que se meter na decisão do candidato do PL à Presidência da República de deixar o país, pois não se trata de uma questão política.

Nesta terça-feira (27), durante a comemoração de seu aniversário, Lula criticou Flávio Bolsonaro por ter "fugido" do país.

Ele lembrou ter sido convidado a também deixar o Brasil quando estava para ser condenado pela Força Tarefa da Lava Jato, mas que decidiu permanecer aqui e enfrentar a prisão, onde ficou 580 dias. Depois, o presidente falou que o momento é de pacificar o país e não gerar mais turbulências.

Segundo seus interlocutores, Lula precisa focar na segunda parte de sua fala, buscando realmente pacificar o país.

Para eles, ficar criticando Flávio Bolsonaro não irá contribuir em nada, pelo contrário, vai atiçar os bolsonaristas contra seu governo. "A hora é de buscar paz para começar um quarto mandato que, pela questão fiscal, não será fácil no início", disse ao blog um desses conselheiros do presidente.

Esses interlocutores lembram que a "fuga" de Flávio Bolsonaro vai dividir a oposição. Ficar criticando o senador do PL só serve para dar mais força para ele tentar, dos Estados Unidos, manter mobilizados em torno dele os bolsonaristas. Ou seja, é melhor deixar que a própria oposição se vire com o caso Flávio Bolsonaro.

Os primeiros pronunciamentos do governador de São Paulo, Tarcísio Gomes de Freitas (Republicanos), e de Michelle Bolsonaro, por sinal, já indicaram que eles pretendem assumir a liderança da oposição.

Enquanto isso, o coordenador da campanha do PL, senador Rogério Marinho, não escondeu sua frustração pela decisão de Flávio Bolsonaro de deixar o país neste momento.

Segundo líderes do PL, a saída de Flávio Bolsonaro vai prejudicar ainda mais a intenção do partido de assumir a presidência do Senado. Se a derrota do Flávio Bolsonaro já havia tirado força de um nome do PL na disputa pela sucessão de Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP), agora, com sua saída do país, tudo fica mais difícil ainda.

Tanto que, ontem mesmo, o PP e o União Brasil já divulgaram nota apoiando a reeleição do atual presidente do Senado.

articles.title: Jair Bolsonaro pede a Moraes para receber Valdemar Costa Neto | G1
articles.standfirst: Pedido ocorre após saída de Flávio Bolsonaro do país. Senador derrotado nas urnas chegou com a família a Miami na manhã desta quarta (28). Resultado das eleições foi atestado pelo TSE, sem qualquer indício de fraudes.
articles.summary: Jair Bolsonaro solicita a Alexandre de Moraes autorização para receber Valdemar Costa Neto após Flávio Bolsonaro deixar o país em meio a investigações no STF.
articles.body:
Presidente nacional do PL, Valdemar Costa Neto — Foto: Beto Barata/PL/Divulgação

A defesa do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro (PL) pediu, nesta quarta-feira (28), que o ministro Alexandre de Moraes, do Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ), autorize uma visita do presidente do PL, Valdemar Costa Neto , a ele, "em razão da necessidade de diálogo direto".

O pedido foi feito após Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), candidato à Presidência derrotado nas urnas no último domingo (28), deixar o país sem entregar seus passaport es conforme determinado por Moraes.

Bolsonaro cumpre prisão domiciliar em Brasília pela condenação a 27 anos e três meses de prisão por tramar um golpe de Estado no país.

Em julho, Moraes proibiu visitas com finalidade político eleitoral até o fim das eleições.

A medida foi adotada após Flávio Bolsonaro divulgar uma carta do pai nas redes sociais, sendo que uma das medidas cautelares impostas a ele proíbe a utilização de plataformas, inclusive por meio de terceiros.

Moraes já negou pedidos de visitas de Valdemar sob argumento de que o presidente do PL ainda continua investigado na trama golpista.

Nesta terça (27), Valdemar recebeu a senadora eleita Michelle Bolsonaro (PL). Em uma postagem numa rede social, o chefe do PL afirmou que trataram do futuro e desafios da legenda.

"Recebi hoje a senadora eleita Michelle Bolsonaro para uma conversa sobre o futuro do nosso partido e os desafios que temos pela frente. Seguimos unidos, com diálogo, responsabilidade e compromisso com o Brasil", diz o texto.

Flávio Bolsonaro chegou a Miami, nos Estados Unidos, com a família na manhã desta quarta. Ele deixou o país apesar da proibição do STF.

O senador perdeu as eleições no último domingo (25) contra o atual presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT). O resultado das eleições foi confirmado pelo ministro Kassio Nunes Marques, presidente do TSE, sem qualquer indício de fraudes.

Flávio Bolsonaro é alvo de investigações na Corte . Ele e o advogado Willer Tomaz são investigados por lavagem de dinheiro, em um suposto esquema que envolveria empresas do jurista e apostas esportivas. O caso segue em sigilo de justiça.

Além disso, o filho do ex-presidente também é formalmente investigado em inquérito aberto para apurar a possível prática de crimes relacionados ao financiamento da produção do filme "Dark Horse", sobre a trajetória de Jair Bolsonaro.

articles.title: Acidente de trem na Espanha deixa 64 mortos; Itamaraty se manifesta | G1
articles.standfirst: Colisão entre veículos deixou pelo menos 64 mortos e 80 feridos na linha que liga Madri à região da Andaluzia, no sul do país.
articles.summary: Itamaraty monitora a situação de brasileiros após colisão de trens na Espanha que deixou 64 mortos e 80 feridos na linha entre Madri e a região da Andaluzia.
articles.body:
O Ministério das Relações Exteriores (Itamaraty) divulgou um comunicado nesta quarta-feira (28) lamentando o acidente ferroviário que deixou centenas de pessoas mortas na Espanha.

A causa do acidente e o número de feridos ainda estão sendo apurados, mas a porta-voz do governo local, da região de Castilla La Mancha, Ester Padilla, confirmou que ao menos 64 pessoas morreram e 80 ficaram feridas.

O governo brasileiro informou que está monitorando a situação pelos Consulados-Gerais do Brasil na Espanha , para prestar a assistência consular cabível a brasileiros eventualmente afetados pela colisão dos trens.

Ainda não se sabe se há brasileiros entre os mortos e feridos.

"O Brasil manifesta sua solidariedade ao povo e ao governo da Espanha, transmite suas sinceras condolências às famílias das vítimas e deseja pronta recuperação aos feridos."

Segundo a porta-voz, um trem da Renfe, com 397 pessoas a bordo, e um trem da Iryo, com 147 passageiros, colidiram pouco depois das 9h do horário local — 5h de Brasília —, entre as cidades de Mora e Orgaz, causando o descarrilamento de vagões.

Equipes de resgate trabalham no local da colisão entre dois trens de alta velocidade, entre as cidades de Mora e Orgaz, perto de Toledo, na Espanha, em 28 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: REUTERS/Violeta Santos Moura

Imagens da emissora regional Castilla La Mancha Television mostram o trem da Iryo descarrilado, com alguns vagões da frente ainda sobre os trilhos, enquanto metal retorcido, painéis quebrados e destroços podem ser vistos espalhados por um aterro abaixo da linha férrea.

Segundo uma fonte ouvida pela agência de notícias Reuters, o trem operado pela Iryo estava parado perto de Toledo por ordem da Adif, empresa gestora da infraestrutura ferroviária, devido a uma falha de sinalização, quando foi atingido pelo trem da Renfe.

As duas empresas ainda não responderam aos pedidos de comentários da Reuters, e a circulação ferroviária está interrompida entre Madrid, Ciudad Real e Andalucía.

articles.title: Flávio Bolsonaro: saída do Brasil e o futuro da direita | G1
articles.standfirst: Saída de senador do país reforça suspeitas sobre autoproteção e abre espaço para uma direita sem o bolsonarismo. Lideranças ouvidas pelo blog veem em Tarcísio de Freitas uma nova liderança para o movimento e citam nova composição do Senado.
articles.summary: Saída de Flávio Bolsonaro do país reforça suspeitas de autoproteção contra investigações e sinaliza uma reorganização da direita. Fontes citam preferência por Tarcísio de Freitas.
articles.body:
A saída de Flávio Bolsonaro do Brasil, cerca de 48h após a derrota nas eleições, na última terça-feira (27), reforça a avaliação de que sua candidatura à Presidência também tinha um objetivo de autoproteção, em busca de blindagem diante das investigações que envolvem o senador.

Segundo relatos de pessoas ligadas a Flávio, ouvidas pelo blog , ele dizia até segunda-feira à noite que permaneceria no país para liderar a oposição. A mudança de planos surpreendeu aliados e deixou sem resposta o que será feito com os quase 60 milhões de votos que ele recebeu no segundo turno.

Há duas frentes de investigação que precisam ser acompanhadas. Uma delas envolve o Master, o financiamento de 'Dark Horse' e o fundo Havengate, nos Estados Unidos.

Investigadores ouvidos pelo blog apontam a necessidade de esclarecer a origem e o destino do dinheiro e apurar eventuais crimes como lavagem de dinheiro, corrupção passiva, entre outros. Havengate, inclusive, significa "refúgio".

A outra envolve o advogado Willer Tomaz, personagem considerado fundamental para entender as relações políticas e financeiras que cercam o senador. É impossível falar do advogado Willer Tomaz sem falar de Flávio Bolsonaro. Todo mundo que cobre política em Brasília sabe disso.

A saída de Flávio também abre espaço para uma reorganização da direita sem o protagonismo da família Bolsonaro.

O governador de São Paulo, Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos), por exemplo, já soltou um vídeo defendendo que a política siga em frente. Um aceno claro a 2030. Até porque não existe espaço vazio na política — e o próximo ciclo já começou.

Essa direita foi sequestrada pela família Bolsonaro — e se deixou virar refém. Antes da saída de Flávio para os EUA, a pergunta era como articular uma nova liderança na direita diante dos 60 milhões de votos depositados no senador. Agora, o caminho parece livre.

Lideranças da direita ouvidas pelo blog já discutem o dia seguinte sem o bolsonarismo e veem em Tarcísio um possível nome para liderar esse movimento. A nova composição do Senado também estará no centro das articulações, em um Congresso eleito com perfil majoritariamente à direita.

Flávio Bolsonaro fala após derrota para Lula no 2º turno — Foto: Adriano Machado/Reuters

articles.title: Morre aos 83 anos empresário Eduardo Paes Mendonça | G1
articles.standfirst: Ele era irmão do também empresário João Carlos Paes Mendonça e faleceu na terça (27), no Recife.
articles.summary: Ele era irmão do também empresário João Carlos Paes Mendonça e faleceu na terça (27), no Recife.
articles.body:
O empresário José Eduardo Paes Medonça morreu aos 83 anos, na terça-feira (27), no Recife ( veja vídeo acima ). Ele era irmão de João Carlos Paes Mendonça, presidente do Grupo JCPM, e era conhecido por sua atuação na rede de supermercados Bompreço e pela criação de iniciativas sociais, como a Casa Sorrir.

Eduardo Mendonça, que faleceu de causas naturais, nasceu em Serra do Machado, em Sergipe, mas morou a maior parte da vida em Pernambuco. Além de ter dirigido o Bompreço, ele também presidiu a aintiga Gráfica JC, rebatizada de Intergraf.

Ele também se dedicou ao ramo de empreendimentos imobiliários e de shopping center, tendo participação nos shoppings Recife, Tacaruna, Guararapes, RioMar Recife, RioMar Fortaleza, RioMar Presidente Kennedy e Salvador Shopping, além de uma empresa de investimentos no mercado internacional.

O empresário também era responsável pelo Instituto José Eduardo Mendonça, conhecido como Casa Sorrir.

Fundada em 2018, a organização funciona no bairro da Ilha do Leite, no Centro do Recife, e oferece apoio para crianças em tratamento da fissura lábiopalatina, uma má-formação congênita que ocorre quando os tecidos do lábio superior ou do céu da boca não se desenvolvem completamente.

Eduardo Mendonça descobriu a má-formação aos 69 anos, e decidiu fundar o instituto como forma de contribuir socialmente com aqueles que conviviam com a mesma condição.

José Eduardo deixa a esposa, Ana Maria Santa Rita, três filhos, Danielle, Eduardo e Viviane, e sete irmãos.

O velório e cremação ocorrem nesta quarta-feira (28), no Cemitério Morada da Paz, em Paulista, no Grande Recife.

O presidente João Carlos Paes Mendonça lamentou a morte do irmão;

José Eduardo era homem de muitos amigos e de uma leveza que agregava as pessoas em torno dele;

Como diretor no Bompreço, liderou o time com confiança e com o sentimento de todos lutarem pelos mesmos desafios.

A governadora Raquel Lyra (PSD) também lamentou a morte e disse que Eduardo Paes Mendonça"contribuiu para o desenvolvimento do nosso estado numa trajetória marcada pela atuação em diversos segmentos".

"Em nome de Ana, sua esposa, filhos, netos e seu irmão, João Carlos Paes Mendonça, expresso minha solidariedade e rezo para que Deus, em sua infinita misericórdia, console os corações de seus familiares e inúmeros amigos neste momento de despedida", disse.

articles.title: Homem é preso por matar cadela a facadas em Presidente Figueiredo | G1
articles.standfirst: Empreendedora Raquel Ferreira, que mora perto do local onde o animal foi morto, contou que a cadela esteve em seu estabelecimento horas antes do ataque.
articles.summary: Após confessar o crime, o homem foi preso com a faca usada no ataque contra o animal, que era cuidado pela comunidade, e responderá por maus-tratos a animais.
articles.body:
Um homem de 18 anos foi preso em flagrante na terça-feira (27), suspeito de matar uma cadela a facadas em Presidente Figueiredo , no interior do Amazonas. Segundo apuração da Rede Amazônica, o animal não tinha dono e era alimentado por moradores da região.

Após o ataque, a Polícia Militar foi acionada e fez buscas para localizar o suspeito. Ele foi encontrado e abordado pelos policiais. Durante a revista, os militares encontraram uma faca que teria sido usada no crime.

Segundo o sargento Lischt, que atendeu à ocorrência, o homem confessou ter atacado a cadela. "De imediato, fomos atrás e conseguimos alcançar o infrator. Durante a abordagem encontramos a faca que supostamente foi usada no crime e, durante a conversa, questionado se ele teria furado a cadela com a faca, ele disse que realmente tinha cometido esse crime", afirmou o policial.

A empreendedora Raquel Ferreira, que mora perto do local onde o animal foi morto, contou que a cadela esteve em seu estabelecimento horas antes do ataque. Segundo ela, o animal comeu ração que havia sobrado de sua gata.

"Ela veio pela manhã, quando eu abri meu comércio ela entrou. Tinha sobrado um pouquinho de ração de minha gata e ela comeu", disse.

Moradores relataram que a cadela nunca havia atacado ninguém.

Após a prisão, o suspeito foi levado para o 37º Distrito Integrado de Polícia (DIP). Ele deve passar por audiência de custódia e responder por maus-tratos a animais.

A legislação brasileira prevê pena de reclusão para quem pratica maus-tratos contra cães e gatos.

articles.title: Motta diz que Câmara vai debater mudança para sistema distrital misto | G1
articles.standfirst: Modelo combina votos em distritos com os votos em listas de partidos e, segundo presidente da Câmara, seria totalmente implementado em 2034. Motta recebeu presidentes de partidos para tratar dos temas nesta quarta (28).
articles.summary: Proposta de Hugo Motta prevê sistema distrital misto em 2034. Câmara também deve criar grupo de trabalho para definir regras da propaganda eleitoral nas redes sociais em 15 dias.
articles.body:
Hugo Motta reúne presidentes de partidos para tratar de mudança no sistema eleitoral — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

O presidente da Câmara, Hugo Motta ( Republicanos -PB), anunciou nesta quarta-feira (28) que a Casa vai abrir debates para alterar o sistema eleitoral proporcional brasileiro para o modelo distrital misto, com implementação definitiva prevista para 2034 .

🔎O sistema distrital misto combina a escolha de parlamentares por votação majoritária nos distritos locais com a distribuição de vagas por votação em listas partidárias pré-ordenadas.

🔎No sistema proporcional atual, as cadeiras do Legislativo são distribuídas aos partidos conforme o total de votos recebidos pela legenda e por seus candidatos (quociente eleitoral), sendo ocupadas pelos nomes mais votados de cada sigla.

Além disso, a Câmara criará um grupo de trabalho para elaborar, em até duas semanas, regras para a propaganda eleitoral em plataformas digitais e redes sociais .

As diretrizes foram definidas durante reunião com dirigentes e parlamentares de siglas de centro e com a presença dos presidentes do Republicanos, Marcos Pereira ; Podemos , Renata Abreu; do União Brasil , Antonio Rueda; e do PSD , Gilberto Kassab . O presidente do PSB , João Campos , também participou.

A meta é iniciar a discussão e, eventualmente, se houver consenso, realizar a votação no plenário ainda neste ano.

Segundo Motta, a implementação deve ser feita a médio prazo para vencer "resistências" no Congresso :

Em 2030, a eleição servirá como etapa intermediária com um modelo de transição, cujos detalhes técnicos ainda serão debatidos com as bancadas;

Em 2034, vigência plena nas eleições para o Legislativo.

A mudança, se aprovada, alcançará Câmara dos Deputados , assembleias legislativas e câmaras de vereadores, sem alterações no modelo majoritário, ou seja, as cadeiras da Presidência da República, governos estaduais, prefeituras e Senado.

🔎O sistema distrital misto busca equilibrar a representação regional e a proporcionalidade partidária.

"Nós temos também a consciência de que precisaremos levar em consideração uma Proposta de Emenda à Constituição (PEC). Nós queremos fazer essa construção por PEC, pois ela traz mais segurança jurídica e, claro, mais legitimidade do ponto de vista do Parlamento para fazer uma mudança estruturante", afirmou Hugo Motta.

O presidente da Câmara destacou que, a partir do consenso firmado com o bloco de centro, vai procurar os partidos da esquerda — como a federação PT/PCdoB/PV, o PSOL e a Rede — e da direita — como o PL e o Novo.

Ele também disse que terá uma reunião nesta quarta com o presidente do Senado, Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP), para tratar de um alinhamento prévio. Ele declarou que o fato de a medida se restringir à escolha proporcional, ou seja, não atinge senadores, facilita o entendimento entre as duas Casas.

Motta também anunciou a vontade dos partidos de modernizar o Código Eleitoral para disciplinar o uso das redes sociais nas campanhas.

Um grupo de trabalho com um representante de cada partido terá 15 dias para elaborar um texto final. A intenção é acelerar a discussão para possibilitar a aprovação da matéria na Câmara e no Senado ainda este ano.

"Nós sabemos hoje que a propaganda eleitoral tem regra no que diz respeito ao material físico, tem regra no que diz respeito às TVs, às rádios. Entendemos que, nas redes sociais e plataformas, precisamos também ter regras claras que garantam paridade de armas e um sistema transparente e isonômico", declarou.

Motta disse que a iniciativa não pretende "tolher absolutamente ninguém", nem "censurar" manifestações nas plataformas digitais.

O objetivo, segundo o deputado paraibano, é garantir previsibilidade e transparência para evitar que candidatos ou legendas obtenham vantagens desproporcionais.

articles.title: Comerciantes são alvo de listas que incentivam boicote em Teresópolis | G1
articles.standfirst: Caso gerou debate na Câmara de Vereadores e motivou representação ao Ministério Público; documento cita situações semelhantes em Petrópolis, Três Rios e Cachoeiras de Macacu.
articles.summary: Caso gerou debate na Câmara de Vereadores e motivou representação ao Ministério Público; documento cita situações semelhantes em Petrópolis, Três Rios e Cachoeiras de Macacu.
articles.body:
Comerciantes e profissionais de Teresópolis , na Região Serrana do Rio, têm sido alvo de publicações em redes sociais e grupos de mensagens que identificam estabelecimentos supostamente ligados a apoiadores do Partido dos Trabalhadores (PT) e incentivam consumidores a não comprar nesses locais.

A repercussão levou o caso à Câmara de Vereadores e motivou uma representação apresentada ao Ministério Público do Estado do Rio de Janeiro (MPRJ) e ao Ministério Público do Trabalho (MPT).

Além de Teresópolis, a representação cita registros semelhantes em Petrópolis , Três Rios e Cachoeiras de Macacu . Entre os exemplos mencionados estão grupos e publicações intitulados “Estabelecimentos Petista em Três Rios” e “Cachoeiras Consciente (não compre de petista)”.

As listas são acompanhadas de mensagens que incentivam o boicote econômico a comerciantes e profissionais associados a determinado posicionamento político. Entre as expressões identificadas está “Não compre de petista”, utilizada em publicações que expõem nomes de estabelecimentos e seus proprietários.

A representação foi apresentada pelo deputado estadual Yuri Moura e solicita a apuração de possíveis práticas de perseguição e discriminação político-partidária. O documento pede a investigação da origem e da autoria das publicações, além de possíveis ameaças, constrangimentos, discriminação e uso irregular de dados pessoais.

A divulgação das listas levantou questionamentos sobre os limites da manifestação política, o direito à liberdade de opinião e os possíveis prejuízos econômicos e profissionais para as pessoas identificadas.

O episódio ocorre em meio à polarização política após as eleições de 2026. Em Teresópolis, Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) recebeu 62,80% dos votos válidos no primeiro turno e ampliou o percentual no segundo turno . Nesse contexto, a circulação das listas passou a preocupar comerciantes que temem ser prejudicados por posicionamentos políticos atribuídos a eles.

Na representação encaminhada ao MPRJ e ao MPT, Yuri Moura também cita a possibilidade de encaminhamento de informações à Autoridade Nacional de Proteção de Dados (ANPD) e ao Conselho Administrativo de Defesa Econômica (Cade), caso sejam encontrados elementos que justifiquem a atuação dos órgãos.

A representação ressalta que o pedido de investigação não significa que as irregularidades apontadas tenham sido comprovadas. Caberá aos órgãos competentes analisar os registros e apurar eventuais responsabilidades.

O caso também foi debatido na Câmara Municipal de Teresópolis. Durante a discussão, vereadores apontaram preocupação com possíveis impactos sobre a liberdade de opinião, a atividade comercial e a convivência democrática.

A repercussão levou diferentes instituições a se manifestarem. A Prefeitura de Teresópolis, a Câmara de Vereadores e o Sindicato do Comércio Varejista de Teresópolis (Sincomércio) repudiaram as práticas denunciadas.

O Partido dos Trabalhadores orientou pessoas que tenham sido ameaçadas ou coagidas a registrar ocorrência policial. Já o Partido Liberal (PL) informou que estava apurando a situação e que não se manifestaria sobre o caso.

Procurado pelo g1 , o Ministério Público do Trabalho informou ter recebido mais de 400 denúncias relacionadas a situações semelhantes em todo o país. Segundo o órgão, todas as denúncias serão investigadas. O MPT também disponibiliza um canal para registro de ocorrências em seu site oficial.

O Ministério Público do Estado do Rio de Janeiro também foi procurado para comentar o caso e informar se havia alguma providência em andamento, mas não havia respondido até a última atualização desta reportagem.

A apuração busca esclarecer a origem das listas, a eventual participação de responsáveis pela divulgação e a existência de ameaças, constrangimentos ou outras condutas que possam gerar responsabilização.

articles.title: STF diz que não há ordem para buscas em endereço de Flávio | G1
articles.standfirst: Senador deixou o país após ordem para a entrega de seus passaportes.
articles.summary: Senador deixou o país após ordem para a entrega de seus passaportes.
articles.body:
O Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) informou, em nota nesta quarta-feira (28), que não há mandado de busca e apreensão direcionado ao senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e seus endereços.

"Não há nenhuma decisão judicial nesse sentido, tampouco realização de diligência policial ou de busca e apreensão", diz a nota.

(CORREÇÃO: O g1 errou ao informar, em uma reportagem publicada em outubro de 2026, que o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) foi alvo de um mandado de busca e apreensão em seu endereço em Brasília. Na verdade, o Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) não autorizou ação da Polícia Federal contra o senador. A matéria foi atualizada às 7h25 de 28/10/2026. Leia mais aqui )

Flávio Bolsonaro deixou o país nessa terça-feira (27). A saída do país aconteceu depois que o ministro Alexandre de Moraes determinou a entrega dos passaportes do parlamentar.

Flávio Bolsonaro e sua família viajavam para os Estados Unidos na manhã desta quarta-feira (28). Seu voo partiu da Argentina, teve breve escala no Equador e seguiu com destino a Miami.

O voo de Flávio e sua família decolou às 6h22, no horário de Brasília, e segue rumo aos EUA, onde está previsto para chegar ao aeroporto Opa-locka Executive, em Miami, por volta das 10h40, segundo o site de monitoramento aéreo FlightAware.

O governo dos EUA afirmou na terça-feira (27) que emitirá vistos para Flávio e sua família e permitirá que eles entrem no país. Nas últimas horas, o presidente Donald Trump voltou a afirmar, sem provas, em fraude na eleição brasileira —que Flávio perdeu para Lula— e disse também que aprovava a ida do senador aos EUA.

As investigações contra Flávio Bolsonaro

Flávio Bolsonaro é alvo de investigações que tramitam no STF. Os casos envolvem suspeitas de irregularidades no financiamento de um filme sobre o ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro, chamado de "Dark Horse", e de lavagem de dinheiro em negócios relacionados a Willer Tomaz.

Em uma das apurações, sob relatoria do ministro André Mendonça, Flávio é investigado pela possível prática de crimes relacionados ao financiamento da produção do filme "Dark Horse", sobre a trajetória do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro.

A investigação mira repasses de Daniel Vorcaro, ex-dono do Banco Master, à produção.

Outra investigação que tramita no STF, sob relatoria do ministro Alexandre de Moraes, apura se o senador cometeu o crime de lavagem de dinheiro, usando uma casa de apostas.

A Polícia Federal (PF) quebrou o sigilo telemático do advogado Willer Tomaz, amigo de Flávio, e encontrou e-mails que apontavam que o senador foi cadastrado como "usuário master" de uma conta bancária da empresa Alcazar Holdings, de propriedade de Tomaz.

A PF afirma no seu relatório que há "elementos indicativos de vínculo de controle ou propriedade de fato de Willer Tomaz sobre a Rede Loto", a primeira a obter autorização estadual da Loterj, no Rio de Janeiro, para explorar apostas esportivas de cota fixa no estado.

articles.title: Blog: Flávio despista escolta do Senado e viaja para os EUA | G1
articles.standfirst: Senador teria deixado de informar a agenda do dia seguinte e não foi localizado pelos agentes responsáveis por sua segurança; chegada aos Estados Unidos ocorreu na manhã desta quarta-feira (28).
articles.summary: Flávio Bolsonaro chegou a Miami após despistar a escolta do Senado. O avião, que saiu da Argentina, fez escala no Equador e evitou o espaço aéreo brasileiro.
articles.body:
O senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) teria despistado a própria escolta, fornecida pelo Senado, antes de deixar o Brasil com destino aos Estados Unidos.

O senador e a família chegaram aos Estados Unidos nesta quarta-feira (28). O avião particular utilizado na viagem pousou em um aeroporto de Miami pela manhã.

O episódio, segundo bastidores, indica que os agentes responsáveis pela segurança do parlamentar não sabiam onde ele estava já na manhã de terça-feira (27). Segundo o relato, Flávio avisou na noite de segunda (26) que enviaria sua agenda no dia seguinte, para que fosse organizada a atuação da equipe de segurança.

Pela manhã, os responsáveis pela escolta tentaram entrar em contato com o senador por telefone, mas não tiveram resposta. Entre 8h e 9h, foram até a residência dele e constataram que Flávio já não estava mais no local.

A sequência levantou a suspeita de que o senador teria evitado deliberadamente o acompanhamento dos agentes do Senado para deixar o país sem que a própria escolta soubesse de seus movimentos.

De acordo com autoridades argentinas, Flávio cruzou a fronteira do Brasil na noite de terça-feira (27) pela Ponte Internacional Tancredo Neves , que liga Foz do Iguaçu a Puerto Iguazú, na província argentina de Misiones.

De lá, embarcou em um avião particular com destino aos EUA e escala em Guaiaquil, no Equador. O trajeto evitou o espaço aéreo brasileiro.

articles.title: Can a Democrat stop Iowa’s red drift? 5 moments from the governor’s debate
articles.summary: Zach Lahn and Rob Sand clash over data center tax breaks, school choice, abortion and gun background checks in Iowa's open governor race.
articles.body: Zach Lahn, a businessman, and Rob Sand, a former Iowa assistant attorney general and two-term state auditor, are competing to succeed retiring Republican Gov. Kim Reynolds, who has served as governor for nearly a decade. The opponents faced off Tuesday night for a 90-minute debate where they discussed fraud, culture wars and data centers, and even found agreement on some issues. The race in Iowa is the state's first open gubernatorial showdown in 20 years, with Reynolds last year announcing she wouldn't seek re-election. Sand, the only Democrat to currently hold statewide office in Iowa, quickly became his party's frontrunner and faced no opposition in this year's primary. Lahn, a self-described entrepreneur and farmer, had to navigate a crowded and contentious primary battle. He won a five-candidate Republican nomination race that included Rep. Randy Feenstra, who was endorsed by President Donald Trump. Sand is aiming to become the first Democrat in two decades elected governor in Iowa, a one-time swing state that's shifted to the right over the past decade. The final Fox News Power Rankings ahead of Election Day rated the race between Lahn and Sand as Lean Democrat. Here are the top five moments. DRAG QUEENS, TRANS PASTOR, ABORTION RALLIES: INSIDE DEM GOVERNOR HOPEFUL'S PROGRESSIVE CHURCH Abortion and Culture War Issues The candidates differed on several culture war issues, such as abortion, parental rights and childhood transgender concerns. Sand affirmed that he would refuse to sign any new bill that he deemed culturally "divisive." "The divisive stuff that people don’t agree on, let’s end that," Sand said. "So vetoing culture war bills to me is just a different way to say I want us to put 100% of our legislating time into issues that impact 100% of Iowans." Sand also said that there is pressure from Republicans and the right to implement greater restrictions on abortion, even though the state has already implemented a six-week ban. "It’s incredibly restrictive," Sand said. "I do not think we have to go further but a lot of the folks in the legislature said when that ban became law that they want to go further. I would veto going further." Meanwhile, Lahn said he is "100%" behind culture battles being fought by conservatives. "There is an issue with these ideologies infiltrating into our culture and I think parents, especially when we talk about some of these issues coming up in schools, they’re just looking for something they should be able to count on. And I think it is absolutely important that we put every single protection in place to make that our daughters are protected, that girls are protected, that women’s sports are protected," Lahn said. Lahn also said that he was motivated to run for office to protect the most vulnerable. "That's the lives of the unborn. That’s our daughters. That’s the young kids in school," Lahn said. MEDICAID PROVIDER ALLEGEDLY BILLED $165K FOR DEAD PATIENT'S RIDES AMONG FRAUD EXPOSED IN EXPLOSIVE REPORT Fraud and Oversight Fraud and improper spending of taxpayer dollars was top of mind for both Lahn and Sand, but the candidates differed in their approaches to tackling corruption. Sand, who used to be the state's auditor, pushed for mandated audits on the state's Education Savings Account program, calling it "common sense." "They're not required to have audits, and they need to have rules for how that money gets spent," Sand said. "Same things that would get you in trouble as a public school should get you in trouble as a private school if you're taking public money. If you don't want to abide by those rules, then you can continue to not take public money." Lahn said during his time as auditor he saw payments being made to dead people and accused Gov. Reynolds of signing a law known as Senate File 478, claiming it made it harder for auditors to do their job. "They changed the law to make it harder for us to find misspent tax money," Sand said. "This is something that every single government watchdog in America that weighed in on said would be a terrible law that would lead to an increase in waste, fraud and abuse." Meanwhile, Lahn maintained that schools should be audited by third parties instead of being under government oversight. "I think third-party auditing is where it should go," Lahn said. "I think we could do something very similar, which allows these schools to still have their privacy, but make sure that the funds are being spent properly." Lahn also raised concerns of improper Medicaid payments, pointing to the fraud allegations from Minnesota's state program. He argued for implementing advanced technologies like blockchain to ensure that money is being properly spent. "This would create thousands of citizen auditors trying to find every single dollar that the government is wasting. And we start at the state level. Then we go down to the county level as well, where we can have radical transparency in spending," Lahn said. "We all want to have more efficient government. One of the best ways to do it is through radical transparency." DEMOCRATS AIM TO KILL SCHOOL CHOICE FROM WISCONSIN TO THE REST OF THE US School Choice Iowa's Education Savings Account program, which provides taxpayer dollars to families to cover tuition for private schools, faced scrutiny by Sand, who called for income restrictions on the program, pointing to the state facing a $1.1 billion deficit. "We are putting hundreds of millions of dollars every single year into the pockets of people who have plenty of money, good for them, and are already going to send their kids to private school, fine by me, but your tax dollars don’t need to go pay for that," Sand said. Lahn argued that the program was a "foundational freedom" and that when a school program isn't meeting a child's needs, parents should be able to go elsewhere regardless of their income. "I think that there's no such thing as government money," Lahn said. "There's the people's money, this is their money." The candidates also disagreed over whether private schools that receive public funding should be allowed to turn away students — an issue the Supreme Court will consider this term in St. Mary Catholic Parish v. Roy, a case from Colorado. "Private schools that are taking public money should have to take whichever students say they want to attend there," Sand said. "The fact that they don’t have to right now exposes the gulf between the rhetoric around this program and what it actually does, because right now, private schools can pick and choose which students can come in the front door." Lahn said the "best model" is for parents to have different options for what fits their child's needs best. "If you put these restrictions on schools, many of them, especially the smallest ones, will be burdened to a great degree," Lahn said. Data Centers Sand and Lahn both agreed that data centers need to pay their "fair share" if they want to build in Iowa. The topic of data centers — which has become a flashpoint issue this election cycle — was first raised by Sand when discussing his plan for balancing the state's budget was to cease giving data companies tax breaks. "Data centers should be paying all their taxes and then some," Sand said. "If they need to build the grid out to do what they need to do, they can pay for that." "Financially speaking, they should be contributing to the state of Iowa, and if they don't want to contribute, they can build somewhere else," Sand continued. Lahn said that he agreed with his opponent, noting it may be "the one thing" that they both agreed on. "A hundred billion dollar multinational company does not need welfare from the people of Iowa," Lahn said. He said that there was a data center receiving $529 million in property tax abatements and was only required to create 30 jobs to receive the tax break. "Not only is this happening too quickly with data centers, but it's also happening in a way that we feel like we're being take advantage of," Lahn said. "What they need to do is pay their fair share, and we need to actually create a new class of property tax, which would be above industrial, because these are employing far fewer people per square foot, and we need to have a higher rate of property, a property tax there," Lahn said. Gun Control To end the debate, the moderators asked Lahn and Sand, who both have pledged support for protecting Second Amendment rights, if there was any legislation that they would sign to restrict or regulate firearms. Lahn shared that he's not in favor of signing any new restrictions, saying the state is in a "good place." Sand said that it's important for law-abiding citizens to be able to exercise their Second Amendment rights, but that he supported background checks. The question comes weeks after three children were gunned down in an elementary school in Oregon. Lahn pointed out that the school shooter was killed by a parent, who had a concealed carry permit. "I think that the last thing we want to do is restrict the ability for lawful citizens that are carrying firearms to protect the people they love in their communities. That's something that we need to make sure we're protecting," Lahn said. Sand shared a story about how he, while prosecuting a man who was out on bail, learned the man had received a concealed carry permit. articles.title: DSA-affiliated Senate nominee sparks bipartisan uproar with comments on communist dictatorship
articles.summary: Angie Nixon's response to whether Cuba is a dictatorship drew sharp rebukes from Democrats and Republicans alike.
articles.body: Florida Democratic Senate nominee Angie Nixon is facing a wave of criticism over her response to a seemingly straightforward question about whether Cuba is a dictatorship, months after joining the Democratic Socialists of America as she campaigns for statewide office in a state shaped by generations of Cuban exiles. "You know, that is what people have told me. I have never been to Cuba, and so I will have to take their word for it," Nixon told CBS News when asked directly whether she considers Cuba a dictatorship. Nixon later pushed back on critics who portrayed her answer as a refusal to acknowledge Cuba's government as a dictatorship, saying she was referring to Cubans she has spoken with who described the country that way and that she believes them. WHO IS ANGIE NIXON? BULLHORN-WIELDING SOCIALIST UPSETS ESTABLISHMENT FAVORITE IN SUNSHINE STATE STUNNER "It's disappointing to have to say this, but CBS News, this is a serious failure of editorial reporting," Nixon wrote on X in response to the network's initial post about the exchange. "I clearly state in this clip that while I have not personally been to Cuba, I have spoken with Cubans who have described it as a dictatorship, and I believe them," she continued. "To claim I declined to answer the question is categorically false. That is not journalism. It is misinformation." CBS subsequently deleted its original post, which had characterized Nixon as declining to say whether Cuba is a dictatorship, and reposted the interview with an editor's note acknowledging that the earlier version "did not accurately portray Rep. Nixon's answer." But Nixon's underlying response still drew criticism from Democrats and Republicans. Among the Democrats criticizing Nixon was Phil Ehr, the party's nominee in Florida's 28th Congressional District, who tied his concerns directly to conversations he said he has had with Cuban-American voters while campaigning in South Florida. VAN JONES WARNS FAR-LEFT SOCIALIST AGENDA IS 'REGRESSIVE' THREAT TO DEMOCRATIC PARTY "I can't get past this after spending a week at early voting sites and seeing firsthand how frightened so many Cuban Americans are," Ehr wrote on X alongside a photo from an early-voting site. "People like this woman thanked us for standing up not only against DSA rhetoric, but for their dignity and humanity." In a separate statement, Ehr called Cuba a "communist dictatorship" and said there was "nothing progressive about making excuses for communist dictatorships." He added that he would "not stand behind Angie Nixon or defend her remarks," declaring, "If the Democratic party is unwilling to condemn them, I will." Ehr was not the only Florida Democrat to object. Elliott Rodriguez, the Democratic nominee in Florida's 27th Congressional District, said that while he and Nixon "agree on many issues," Cuba's status was not among them. "Cuba being a dictatorship is not a matter of opinion. It is a fact," Rodriguez wrote, pointing to political prisoners, repression and Cubans who have died seeking freedom. FLA DEM SEN-NOMINEE ANGIE NIXON BACKED ABOLISHING ELECTORAL COLLEGE, RANKED-CHOICE VOTING IN RESURFACED CLIPS Republicans criticized the exchange as well, including Sen. Rick Scott, R-Fla., who argued Nixon's answer reflected a broader problem within the Democratic Party. "Like many of her Democrat colleagues who can't seem to define what a woman is, we now have a candidate for the U.S. Senate who can't define a dictatorship," Scott wrote on X. Rep. Byron Donalds, R-Fla., was similarly blunt, calling Nixon's response "the craziest thing I've ever heard." "Of COURSE the Castro regime is a dictatorship," Donalds wrote. "It's sad to see what has become of the Democrat Party. They are fully consumed by socialism." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The controversy comes months after Nixon joined the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), a membership that has previously drawn questions about where she stands on the organization's positions involving Cuba. SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER In an August interview with CBS Miami, Nixon was asked specifically about DSA's praise of Fidel Castro and distanced herself from the group's position. "I don't believe he's someone that should be praised," Nixon said, while adding that she does not agree with every position taken by DSA.

articles.title: Dem eyeing Sen comeback to fix ‘broken DC system’ raked in cash from establishment queen: 'Jekyll and Hyde'
articles.summary: Former Democratic Sen. Sherrod Brown accepted $33,000 from Nancy Pelosi despite his vocal crusade against congressional stock trading and corruption.
articles.body: FIRST ON FOX: Former Ohio Democratic Sen. Sherrod Brown has pitched himself as a Washington outsider fighting against a broken system, but records reviewed by Fox News Digital show his campaign pocketed tens of thousands of dollars from Nancy Pelosi, one of the most notable establishment figures in Washington, D.C., whose husband is a prolific stock trader. A vocal critic of members of Congress "who are too busy lining their own pockets" and trading stocks, Brown's campaign has accepted a total of $33,000 from Pelosi-affiliated committees since 2006, including $28,000 since February 2024, according to Federal Election Commission records. Brown has taken a firm stance against congressional stock trading, writing on his campaign website, "No one – NO ONE – who serves in Congress, or their spouse, should be able to trade stocks. They also shouldn’t be able to turn around when they leave office and become a lobbyist. If you can’t agree to that, you shouldn’t be in public office." Just weeks after announcing his comeback bid last year, Brown received $7,000 from committees affiliated with Pelosi. PAC to the Future gave $5,000, while Nancy Pelosi for Congress gave $2,000. WATCH: DEM CANDIDATE GRILLED ON STOCK TRADING AFTER BEING DUPED WITH SELFIE REQUEST Mehek Cooke, a GOP strategist and attorney in Ohio, told Fox News Digital that Brown has always sided with the Democratic establishment and has "never worked for us." "I hate when people present themselves as one thing and then turn their backs on you in Washington," Cooke said, calling it another example of Brown’s "Jekyll and Hyde" platform. She pointed to Brown’s lengthy career in politics as proof that he has been part of a system for "50-plus years" that he frequently condemns. The former House speaker and her husband, Paul Pelosi, have an estimated net worth of roughly $278 million, according to a 2026 Yahoo Finance report. A 2025 New York Post report also found the couple made more than $130 million in stock profits during her congressional career. In a statement to Fox News Digital, Nicholas Martin, a spokesperson for Pelosi, denied she had any involvement in stock trading. "Speaker Pelosi does not own any stocks and has no knowledge or subsequent involvement in any transactions," Martin wrote. Pelosi stood behind lawmakers trading individual stocks during a 2021 press briefing, saying, "We are a free-market economy. They should be able to participate in that," before changing course in early 2022. Last year, Pelosi supported a ban, saying, "We must have strong transparency, robust accountability and tough enforcement for financial conduct in office because the American people deserve confidence that their elected leaders are serving the public interest — not their personal portfolios." FOX NEWS POLL: GENDER GAP AND POCKETBOOK PAIN SHAPE OHIO SENATE RACE Brown’s position comes amid ongoing debate over congressional stock trading, with critics arguing the controversial practice gives lawmakers an unfair advantage. Last month, Senate Democrats blocked a Republican-backed bill, the Stop Insider Trading Act, that would ban lawmakers from trading stocks, arguing it wasn’t strong enough. Brown, recruited to run by Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, is looking to reclaim a seat in the U.S. Senate and will face Republican Sen. Jon Husted in Ohio’s closely watched midterm race. Brown, a former chairman of the Senate Banking Committee, was first elected to the Senate in 2006 before losing his 2024 re-election bid to Sen. Bernie Moreno, R-Ohio. EX-HOUSE DEM WHO RIPPED CONGRESSIONAL STOCK TRADING BAN AS 'BULLS---' CHANGES HER TUNE IN COMEBACK BID This is not the first time Brown has faced questions over his campaign donations. Fox News Digital reported in September that Brown targeted Husted over Ohio’s data centers in a campaign ad featuring a facility owned by Google, despite its PAC and lobbyists donating thousands of dollars to his campaigns. Cooke said Brown will continue accepting money from prominent Democrats like Pelosi rather than fighting "for the working man." "Sherrod Brown's always going to be part of the broken Washington system that President Trump just flipped upside down when he got into office," Cooke said. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Fox News Digital reached out to Brown's campaign for comment. "Sherrod Brown spent 32 years in Washington literally building the system he now calls ‘rigged,’" Husted campaign spokesperson Amy Natoce told Fox News Digital in a statement. "Brown is backed and funded by the same people he claims to oppose — this is just another stunning example of Sherrod Brown’s hypocrisy and the fact that he’s willing to lie to Ohio families."

articles.title: What's next for Ilhan Omar? Former immigration judge breaks down legal risks amid federal probes
articles.summary: A former immigration judge says Ilhan Omar could face denaturalization and criminal charges depending on the federal investigation's findings.
articles.body: MINNEAPOLIS — A former federal immigration judge says Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., who is under investigation, could face both criminal charges and denaturalization. There are two federal probes ongoing into the congresswoman — the first into alleged immigration fraud and the second involving her financial disclosures and a sharp discrepancy reported just one year apart. "If somebody who's a naturalized citizen — which I believe Ilhan Omar is — is convicted of a crime, that doesn't automatically mean that they face denaturalization or anything like that," Nathan Hansen, an attorney of 23 years, told Fox News Digital. "They would be handled by any type of other normal punishment that would come from the court." Hansen was appointed by former Attorney General Pam Bondi to serve as an immigration judge earlier this year. He served in the role for four months. GREGG JARRETT: ILHAN OMAR COULD FACE INDICTMENT, DENATURALIZATION AND DEPORTATION Denaturalization proceedings are separate from any criminal case that could arise from the federal investigation into Omar, whose "real name," according to sources familiar with the investigation, is Ilhan Nur Said Elmi. Omar is under investigation for alleged immigration fraud related to the way she or her late father filled out her citizenship paperwork. "A denaturalization proceeding, or somebody to strip somebody of their naturalization, is another proceeding, which would be a civil proceeding brought by the Department of Justice, presumably maybe on behalf of the Department for Homeland Security, who handles most of these things," said Hansen. HOMAN SAYS ILHAN OMAR COULD BE STRIPPED OF NATURALIZATION, DEPORTED IF IMMIGRATION FRAUD IS PROVEN "If there was some sort of nexus between the criminal conviction and somebody's citizenship, it might be more likely that the Department of Justice would bring a denaturalization proceeding," Hansen continued. "But I think it would be a discretionary matter within the people who are running the Justice Department." Omar's Washington, D.C., home was raided by Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), the principal investigative arm of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), in the early morning hours of Oct. 12. During the raid, investigators reportedly seized the congresswoman's phone, passport and computer. Fox News later confirmed that authorities are in possession of her DNA. Regarding the case, observers have speculated that if indeed Omar has broken the law, statutes of limitations could hinder a prosecution. Hansen has seen those claims but doesn't believe them to be valid. "My view of that is generally that fraud stops any statute of limitations. In other words, if something isn't disclosed or something's hidden, then it would be unfair to the other party to toll a statute of limitations against them," said Hansen. "That's just sort of a general principle of law." articles.title: GOP election losses could scramble year-end funding fight
articles.summary: A bruising midterm election for Republicans could complicate Congress’s next government funding fight, as lawmakers return to Washington facing uncertainty over how President Trump will respond to potential GOP losses. Congress has passed a stopgap measure, also known as a continuing resolution (CR), to keep the government funded through Dec. 11. Lawmakers in both parties…
articles.body:
A bruising midterm election for Republicans could complicate Congress’s next government funding fight, as lawmakers return to Washington facing uncertainty over how President Trump will respond to potential GOP losses.

Congress has passed a stopgap measure, also known as a continuing resolution (CR), to keep the government funded through Dec. 11. Lawmakers in both parties said they expect to pass another short-term measure if they cannot finish work on all 12 appropriations bills — and that the odds of a shutdown remain low.

But the election results could reshape the political dynamics surrounding government funding, with Trump emerging as a wild card in negotiations if Republicans must grapple with the fallout of losing their congressional majority next year.

The final weeks of the year could represent Republicans’ last opportunity to advance some of their top legislative priorities before Democrats potentially take control of the House or Senate.

“I don’t know if there’s going to be a shutdown because I have no idea how crazy Republicans are going to act and the things that they’re going to present that are just going to make working families’ lives more difficult and more unaffordable,” said Rep. Bonnie Watson Coleman (D-N.J.), who sits on the House Appropriations Committee and is retiring at the end of this term. “I don’t know if they’re going to give a darn one way or the other after the election.”

“I suspect that Republicans are very interested in waiting to see what happens on Election Day, and therefore, what climate are they going to operate under. And I think that we should be prepared for some very difficult discussions and difficult maneuvers on the part of the Republicans,” Watson Coleman added.

At the same time, Republicans are pointing the finger at Democrats, arguing the ball is in their court.

“Whether or not there is a government shutdown is entirely up to Senate Democrats, who inflicted the longest government shutdown in U.S. history on the American people last year,” said Rep. Andrew Clyde (R-Ga.), also a member of the Appropriations Committee, in a statement.

“My priority remains passing the most conservative and fiscally responsible appropriations bills possible, and I look forward to completing that work when we return to Washington in the coming weeks,” he added.

Lawmakers will return to Washington on Nov. 9, giving them just two weeks to make progress on government funding before leaving again for Thanksgiving recess, with a crowded legislative agenda that includes the annual National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), a farm bill and other priorities.

The House has passed three of the 12 appropriations bills, while Senate appropriators have remained deadlocked over top-line spending levels. The bills the House has passed so far — funding military construction and the Department of Veterans Affairs, the State Department, and agriculture and rural development — represent some of the lowest-hanging fruit.

Speaker Mike Johnson (R-La.) is sure to face much tougher resistance — both from Democrats and within his party — when the topic shifts to funding other agencies, including the departments of Homeland Security, Defense and Health and Human Services.

The Hill has reached out to House Appropriations Committee Chair Tom Cole (R-Okla.) for comment.

Rep. Nancy Mace (R-S.C.) said in a statement, “We think the odds of a shutdown are low.”

“Congress has made a tradition out of kicking the can down the road until December and passing a Christmas omnibus or continuing resolution,” she said.

Rep. Henry Cuellar (D-Texas), ranking member of the Appropriations Subcommittee on Homeland Security, said Democrats’ position has been to finish all 12 bills rather than pass another CR.

“Now we don’t know how the Republicans are going to react, if they would like to finish it. I hope we can do that, and we’re going to do everything to work something out, so we don’t have another CR. If we have to, we’ll do it, but you know we prefer not to do it, and certainly we don’t want to have a shutdown. I don’t foresee a shutdown, but things have surprised me in Washington,” Cuellar said.

A government shutdown would likely have negative implications for both parties.

“When you have a shutdown, one party thinks they’re winning before they realize that we’re not winning, and then the other side thinks they’re winning before they realize that they were not winning, and that’s what you know makes those shutdowns long and dangerous. But at the end of the day, you know, it’s the American public that loses,” Cuellar said.

House Appropriations Committee ranking member Rosa DeLauro (D-Conn.) told The Hill in a statement she doesn’t think anyone wants a shutdown, and one is not likely.

“Both Democrats and Republicans have expressed a desire to finish full-year funding bills before the end of this calendar year, and I am ready to do just that,” DeLauro said. “The American people want us to address the cost of living crisis and rein in this corrupt administration. With Democrats widely expected to be in the majority, we want to hit the ground running in the new year — not be forced to finish the work this Congress failed to complete.”

articles.title: The Memo: DOJ targets Trump foes in flurry of activity in election’s shadow
articles.summary: FBI agents raided a California home as part of an investigation into former Rep. Eric Swalwell (D-Calif.) on Tuesday, adding to a rapidly lengthening list of law enforcement actions that have a political component, just one week before the midterm elections. The day before, it emerged that the Department of Justice (DOJ) was seeking, for…
articles.body:
FBI agents raided a California home as part of an investigation into former Rep. Eric Swalwell (D-Calif.) on Tuesday, adding to a rapidly lengthening list of law enforcement actions that have a political component, just one week before the midterm elections.

The day before, it emerged that the Department of Justice (DOJ) was seeking, for a third time, to prosecute former FBI Director James Comey, who has had a place near the top of President Trump’s list of foes for almost a decade.

Prior to that, FBI agents searched the Washington-area home of Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-Minn.), apparently as part of an investigation into her family’s immigration process roughly 30 years ago. Meanwhile, two former FBI officials were charged last week , supposedly for downplaying their involvement in probes conducted into then-President Biden’s son Hunter Biden.

Swalwell, Comey, Omar and the two former FBI personnel — Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides — all deny wrongdoing.

Separate from those cases, the DOJ also set off a political firestorm last week when it filed a preemptive suit that could block certification of the result of the U.S. Senate race in Alaska if Democratic candidate Mary Peltola defeats incumbent Sen. Dan S. Sullivan (R) by a narrow margin. The DOJ is taking exception to the presence on the ballot of a similarly named candidate, Dan J. Sullivan, despite the Alaska Supreme Court having already considered the matter.

Trump later told reporters he was the person who told the DOJ to “do it,” in relation to filing the Alaska suit.

Taken together, the developments have raised the ire and anxiety of Trump critics who see the aggregate effect as a weaponization of the justice system for political aims.

They note, among other things, that the DOJ has typically abided by the custom of not taking conspicuous action within 60 days of an election, for fear of being seen to be trying to affect the outcome.

There can be exceptions to this practice — for example, to prevent a planned crime from being committed or to prevent destruction of evidence. But it is far from clear that those issues apply to any of the key cases now.

Meanwhile, the people being accused or investigated face the challenge that they cannot fully dispel suspicion between now and Election Day.

Omar is the only serving politician in the group, and she is not expected to be in any electoral trouble in her heavily Democratic district. But the FBI raid could besmirch Democratic standing with voters more generally, including in the competitive Senate race in Minnesota.

In the interim, Omar is trying to push back against leaks to Trump-friendly media outlets, which have offered varying descriptions of what exactly is being investigated.

Neither Omar nor Swalwell, who resigned from Congress earlier this year, has been charged with any crime.

Comey and the former FBI officials will not have the opportunity to rebut the charges against them at trial — if their cases even proceed that far — until the midterm elections are distant in the rearview mirror.

There are obvious differences between a current Democratic officeholder (Omar), a former lawmaker (Swalwell), and nonparty figures like Comey, Floris and Benavides. But the fear is that all the cases can be pushed together to try to buttress Trump’s frequent allegations that nefarious Democrats and shadowy “Deep State” figures are conspiring to damage him.

Many critics acknowledge it is possible wrongdoing could emerge in some cases.

But they also assert that the current administration cannot expect the presumption of good faith.

They tend to highlight things like the president’s public message last year to then-Attorney General Pam Bondi, urging her to expedite prosecutions of his enemies. The current attorney general, Todd Blanche, told a podcast last week: “They accuse me of not suffering from independence. I don’t. I work for President Trump.”

For administration critics, it’s all ominous stuff.

“I’m actually surprised that it took this long to pursue these types of aggressive actions that smell of political retribution,” said attorney Mark Zaid, who has represented whistleblowers during Democratic and Republican administrations. “That’s not to say there might not be smoke behind the fire. But this administration has set those fires for perceived political reasons.”

Zaid himself fought an attempt earlier in the Trump administration to strip him of his security clearance.

The most high-profile targets are emphatic that the probes they face are political in nature.

Comey in a video on Monday said: “Well, they’re back — again. It would almost be funny if it weren’t such an appalling abuse of the Department of Justice — one that we cannot become numb to.”

Omar’s office issued a statement soon after the raid on her home in which it called the action “an outrageous abuse of power” and added: “No president should be able to use the power of the federal government to intimidate his political enemies.”

Trump, Blanche and other administration figures insist the actions they are taking are just. Trump told reporters Monday he wasn’t aware of the Comey charges before they became public, though he did once again inveigh against the former FBI director as a “dirty cop.”

Susan Del Percio, a Republican strategist but Trump critic, countered that the administration is doing lasting damage.

“The harm that has been inflicted on the institutions will take years to rebuild,” she said.

But Del Percio also argued that any attempt to use the wheels of justice to smooth the GOP’s way in the midterms could backfire.

Recent actions are showing what Trump’s priorities are, she said. “It is retribution, not focusing on the American people. That’s why the president’s numbers are so low.”

The Memo is a reported column by Niall Stanage.

articles.title: Jeffries tiptoes around Hegseth impeachment
articles.summary: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-N.Y.) is tiptoeing around the impeachment of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, denouncing the Pentagon chief in the sharpest terms but without taking the further step of endorsing Hegseth’s forced removal. Jeffries’s careful approach highlights the delicate dance Democratic leaders are attempting as they seek to balance the various interests in…
articles.body:
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-N.Y.) is tiptoeing around the impeachment of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, denouncing the Pentagon chief in the sharpest terms but without taking the further step of endorsing Hegseth’s forced removal.

Jeffries’s careful approach highlights the delicate dance Democratic leaders are attempting as they seek to balance the various interests in their diverse caucus, especially ahead of next week’s elections when the House is theirs to lose.

On one hand, Jeffries wants to take the fight to the Trump administration to appease a liberal base that’s been critical of the party for going too soft on the president in his second term. On the other hand, Democratic leaders also don’t want to lend fuel to President Trump’s claims that a Democratic majority would be hellbent on impeachments and other disciplinary actions against the administration simply to settle old political scores — a perception that could alienate more moderate voters in the midterms.

Squeezed between those competing camps, Jeffries, who’s in line to become Speaker if the House does change hands, has repeatedly sought a middle ground. He’s lambasted Hegseth as grossly unqualified — and called for him to be fired — but stopped short of throwing his weight behind the impeachment push many Democrats want to see.

The latest instance came over the weekend at a campaign rally in New York, where Jeffries vowed that a House Democratic majority would “run Pete Hegseth out of town.”

Asked by reporters afterward to clarify his intentions, Jeffries instead remained vague.

“It means that we’re going to hold him accountable in the same way that we held [former Attorney General] Pam Bondi and [former Homeland Security Secretary] Kristi Noem accountable,” Jeffries said, according to MS NOW . “And Pete Hegseth needs to be pushed aside by the president, or we’re going to have to deal with that situation if he is not.”

Taken literally, the analogy suggests Jeffries doesn’t want to go the impeachment route, since both Bondi and Noem were pushed out of power by Trump — not by Congress — after losing the president’s favor.

One House Democrat, who requested anonymity to weigh in on Jeffries’s approach, guessed the minority leader wants to see how Rep. Thomas Massie’s (R-Ky.) impeachment push plays out first before turning to other possibilities that will also depend on how the elections will shake out.

“I think if there’s an opportunity to be bipartisan, we’re always going to look for that opportunity. I know he [Jeffries] always looks for that opportunity. So, I think we don’t want to take the pressure off,” the Democratic lawmaker said, adding that more Republicans will want to register their frustration with Hegseth post-midterms.

Jeffries won’t be able to remain on the fence much longer.

Last month, Massie had introduced eight articles of impeachment against Hegseth — half of them related to the Iran war. Critically, Massie invoked a special procedure that forces the resolution to the House floor even over the objections of the GOP leaders who control the chamber. Speaker Mike Johnson (R-La.) had altered the House calendar to avoid that vote before the midterms, but it only delayed the inevitable: The vote is expected to happen quickly when lawmakers return to Washington after the elections.

Democratic leaders may feel liberated, at that point, to support Hegseth’s ouster. But if Democrats win the majority, Jeffries will also have to weigh the potential effects of that vote on his broader goal of winning the Speakership, which will require the support of 218 Democrats on the House floor in the first week of January.

But even some Republicans who have been critical of the Pentagon chief are not sold on Massie’s impeachment salvo.

“I’m a little leery about voting for the impeachment. I felt like we’ve been at war with Iran for 47 years. At what point do we not fight back on a country that’s been killing Americans like they’ve done? I’ve had friends killed by these guys by proxy groups,” Rep. Don Bacon (R-Neb.), a retired Air Force brigadier general who is not running for reelection, said in a phone interview with The Hill.

“I also know the Senate will not pass this,” he said. “So what are we going to do? We’re going to take up the rest of the four weeks’ bandwidth to do an impeachment that the Senate won’t vote for.”

Many other Democrats aren’t being so guarded. Those lawmakers have slammed Hegseth in statements, rallies and during appearances on news show, criticizing the Defense secretary for firing more than two dozen senior military officers, overseeing the U.S. military’s campaign of blowing up alleged drug boats in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific, and have accused the Pentagon of not being transparent enough over the war against Iran.

If those aren’t impeachable offenses, they say, then nothing is.

“On HASC [House Armed Services Committee], a top priority should be accountability for Hegseth’s illegal actions in the Caribbean, for the illegal bombings in Iran, and for the illegal firing of generals,” Rep. Ro Khanna (D-Calif.), one of the committee’s members, said in a statement to The Hill, adding that he backs Massie’s impeachment effort.

Hegseth defended his plan to cut 20 percent of admirals and generals — which will affect positions across the Army, Navy and the Air Force — earlier this month, saying they’re “rank-heavy” and out of touch with troops on the ground.

“With more layers and more rank comes more distance between the warfighter and the decisionmaker, and not necessarily better outcomes. In fact, there’s an inverse relationship between success on the battlefield [and] the number of four- and three-star generals since World War II,” the Pentagon chief said on Oct. 1 at the Association of the United States Army in Washington, D.C.

“Pete Hegseth’s name is known widely and held an incredibly low esteem here in my district, and I think across the country. I think people see him for what he is, which is a clown,” said Rep. Pat Ryan (D-N.Y.), another Armed Services Committee member and former Army intelligence officer.

Ryan, a vocal Hegseth critic, said Democrats are looking to dig into Trump’s family members and allies benefiting financially from the Iran war and massive expenditure of offensive and defensive munitions in the U.S. Central Command theater .

The New York Democrat said throughout the last year-and-a-half, he has had relatives of service members as well as Pentagon insiders come forward with “incredibly damning and concerning information” regarding the leadership of the department. He said those people will come forward if the Democrats gain subpoena power after the midterms.

The Pentagon defended Hegseth, calling him a “transformative leader” who brought back standards and merit and now the morale and recruitment inside the military are “at all-time highs.”

“Secretary Hegseth has slashed bureaucracy, unleashed innovation, and delivered for our warfighters every step of the way. By every measurable metric, the Department of War is better under President Trump and Secretary Hegseth’s leadership than before. The entire Department is unified behind the Secretary’s vision and will continue working to put our warfighters and America first,” Kingsley Wilson, the Pentagon’s press secretary, said in a statement.

“At the War Department, we are solely focused on Peace Through Strength and ensuring our warfighters have everything they need to be successful,” Pentagon chief spokesperson Sean Parnell said in a statement. “We are proud to serve our warriors.”

Rep. Adam Smith (D-Wash.), the top Democrat on HASC, again said the Defense secretary was unqualified for the role and called for his removal.

“In all likelihood, yes,” Smith said when asked Tuesday on CNN if he would vote for impeachment. “But I have to look at the particular articles and the particular arguments before I make that commitment.”

Other Democrats on the panel, like Rep. Sara Jacobs (D-Calif.), will vote for Massie’s resolution. Jacobs, who represents San Diego, the country’s biggest military community, confirmed to The Hill that she is for impeaching Hegseth after the midterms if he is still in the role.

Rep. Melanie Stansbury (D-N.M.), who sits on the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, told The Hill she is a “hard yes” on both options.

Rep. Chrissy Houlahan (D-Pa.), a former Air Force captain and member of HASC, expressed the same sentiment.

“I will also wholeheartedly support such an effort in the 120th if he has not resigned or been fired before then,” Houlahan said in a statement.

Rep. Marilyn Strickland (D-Wash.), another HASC member who supports Hegseth’s impeachment, lambasted the Defense secretary for blocking promotions of one- and two-star officers across the Army , Navy and Air Force, warning it jeopardizes the military’s preparedness.

“His blocked promotions threaten our readiness as the war in Iran rages, and is an affront to the highly qualified military officials who are being sidelined,” Strickland said in a statement to The Hill.
